stories.ltme_summary: CCBE has published a notice about Lawyers' Day 2026 in Georgia, an international conference on lawyers and the effective protection of rights in the age of artificial intelligence. The extract is brief and reads as a conference announcement, with a heading on the International Criminal Court. Details of speakers, dates and format are not visible in the extract.
stories.hook: CCBE promotes Lawyers' Day 2026 in Georgia, focused on AI and the protection of rights

SRA 2026/27 Business Plan published
stories.ltme_summary: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has published its final 2026/27 Business Plan, setting out three priorities: operational excellence, proactive risk identification and focusing on the biggest issues. It reports a 45 per cent rise in misconduct reports between 2022 and 2025 and plans a proactive supervision function. Chief executive Sarah Rapson says the plan marks the next stage of the reset.
stories.hook: SRA publishes final 2026/27 business plan with a new proactive supervision function

stories.title: Latham & Watkins devotes $1M to AI program for associates
Democrats’ Midterm Wins Could Reshape Healthcare Access For Underserved Americans
Is Big Law ‘AI Gaslighting’ Us?
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer's opinion piece asks whether large law firms' high-profile AI investments and announcements benefit clients or are mainly marketing. The author suggests firms share measurable client benefits, such as lower fees on AI-assisted matters and faster delivery. The piece is commentary and does not report a new deal or product.
stories.hook: Artificial Lawyer asks whether Big Law's AI spending benefits clients or is marketing

stories.title: Keeping Legal AI Connected: Why Your Data and Case Should Work Together
stories.ltme_summary: Marla Crawford, general counsel at Cimplifi, argues in a guest column that legal teams adding many AI tools risk scattering data and work product across disconnected systems. She says this creates problems for defensibility, control and cost in litigation and eDiscovery. The column promotes Relativity aiR as the system of record where work should come together.
stories.hook: Cimplifi's general counsel says fragmented AI tools in eDiscovery create defensibility and cost risks

stories.title: Paul Weiss Adds Securities Litigator in New York

Gibson Dunn confirms Weil co-managing partner among 120-strong transatlantic funds lift
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that Gibson Dunn has confirmed it has hired a 120-lawyer private funds team from Weil, including 23 partners and Weil co-managing partner Jonathon Soler. The group joins offices in New York, Washington DC and London. The move follows Weil's decision to wind down.
stories.hook: Gibson Dunn confirms 120-lawyer private funds hire from Weil, including co-managing partner Jonathon Soler

stories.title: Freshfields and Goodwin match Milbank scale for US associates
SQE set to generate £59 million in fees as SRA seeks to rebuild confidence in exams
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that the SRA's 2026/27 business plan forecasts £59.1m in education and training income from SQE candidate fees, and £60.9m in spending. The SRA will cut SQE1 questions from 360 to 340 from January 2027. The latest SQE1 overall pass rate was 42 per cent in July, down from 53 per cent in January.
stories.hook: SRA forecasts £59.1m SQE income and cuts SQE1 questions from 360 to 340 from January 2027

stories.title: Dentons posts 90% retention score for trainees and apprentices
The personal injury justice gap: Why injuries are rising but claims are falling in 2026
stories.ltme_summary: National Claims argues that personal injury claims have fallen sharply, citing ACSO figures of 413,323 claims registered in 2025 against more than 876,000 in 2018, a fall of 53 per cent. It cites HSE data on about 680,000 non-fatal workplace injuries in 2024/25 and suggests people may be deterred from claiming.
stories.hook: National Claims says personal injury claims fell 53 per cent since 2018 despite rising injuries

stories.title: Perfect Portal launches new payments service with lower handling charges and greater flexibility
stories.ltme_summary: Perfect Portal has launched One Percent Payments, a payment service built with InfoTrack and powered by Mollie. It charges a 1 per cent handling fee on standard domestic credit and debit card payments, with other methods possibly higher. The service is available to firms using both Perfect Portal and InfoTrack.
stories.hook: Perfect Portal and InfoTrack launch One Percent Payments with a 1 per cent card handling charge

stories.title: SRA to explore “alternative regulatory tools” to investigations
stories.ltme_summary: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has published its final business plan for the year to 31 October 2027. It plans to explore alternatives to formal investigations, such as supervisory dialogue or conditions on authorisations. The plan raises the practising certificate fee share by £50 to £240 to raise an extra £25m, with £23m for IT and change programmes. Misconduct reports rose 45 per cent to 16,499.
stories.hook: SRA plans to use supervision and authorisation conditions in place of some investigations

stories.title: TalkingTech Podcast: New Outlook risks and the rise of open source in legal
stories.hook: TalkingTech podcast turns to Outlook risks and open source in legal technology

stories.title: Simpson Thacher joins Kirkland and Paul Weiss in ending financial disclosures
Legora taps former minister for government push as legal AI moves well beyond law firms
stories.ltme_summary: Legora has appointed former Cabinet minister Lucy Frazer KC to lead its global public sector partnerships, starting with the UK and Europe. Frazer has advised the Swedish company since July. Nonbillable reports that Harvey, Clio and LexisNexis are also courting government customers, and that a Thomson Reuters survey found over a quarter of government legal professionals now use AI.
stories.hook: Legora hires Lucy Frazer KC to lead its push into government and public sector legal work

stories.title: Ex-Clifford Chance lawyer bets on AI agents for in-house legal work
stories.ltme_summary: Claren, founded by former Clifford Chance lawyer Gus Neate, has launched Envoys, AI agents that take in-house legal requests, apply playbooks and escalate to lawyers. Neate says the US is now the fastest-growing market and the company raised $1.7m in pre-seed funding last year. Claren, formerly Wilson AI, says it is not currently seeking new funding.
stories.hook: Claren launches Envoys AI agents to handle incoming in-house legal work

stories.title: Law firms have a new way to measure how good their lawyers are at AI
stories.ltme_summary: Harvey commissioned a five-level AI fluency framework for lawyers, developed by legal AI consultant Peter Duffy of TITANS. It uses platform usage data rather than self-assessment. CMS Netherlands says it took part in the research, and NautaDutilh has referenced the framework in a recruitment advert.
stories.hook: Harvey-commissioned AI fluency framework ranks lawyers from dormant to catalyst

stories.title: Charity forced to close court support services after MoJ funding cut
stories.ltme_summary: Support Through Court, a charity helping people who face civil and family courts without a lawyer, is closing its Chelmsford and Southend services after a £300,000 annual cut in Ministry of Justice funding. Its chief executive, Emma Taylor, says further reductions may become unavoidable without alternative funding. The charity is urging the government to reconsider and has asked supporters to contact MPs and ministers.
stories.hook: Support Through Court closes two Essex services after losing £300,000 a year in Ministry of Justice funding

stories.title: 29% fee rise will bring about 'real change', SRA pledges
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the SRA's 2026/27 business plan lifts the practising certificate fee to £240 from £190 and raises income from practising fees by 29 per cent to £111.5m. Compensation fund contributions rise from £26m to £46.3m. Law Society president Brett Dixon says the extra cost should be short term and called for independent LSB assessment.
stories.hook: SRA plan lifts practising certificate fee to £240 and compensation fund contributions to £46.3m

stories.title: Collapsed firm's staff find new home as 400 files acquired
stories.ltme_summary: Ridley & Hall, a Yorkshire firm, is opening a Harrogate office after acquiring 400 family and property cases from Berwins Solicitors, which appointed administrators the previous week. It has recruited six former Berwins staff, including Michelle Crowhurst and Danielle Day. Managing director Emma Pearmaine says the firm aims for £7m turnover in its centenary year.
stories.hook: Ridley & Hall takes 400 Berwins cases and six staff as it opens a Harrogate office

stories.title: New proposals to stop childhood crimes closing doors for life
stories.ltme_summary: The Ministry of Justice has launched a consultation on ending lifelong disclosure for some childhood convictions, removing disclosure of out-of-court resolutions and reducing disclosure of fines. Serious violent and sexual offences would be excluded. Minister Jake Richards says the plans give young people a fair chance, and the consultation launches ahead of Alan Milburn's review.
stories.hook: MoJ proposes ending lifelong disclosure for some childhood convictions, excluding serious offences

stories.title: Reforming childhood criminal records disclosure
stories.hook: Ministry of Justice consults on reforms to childhood criminal records disclosure until 24 December

stories.ltme_summary: The Institute of Legal Finance & Management (ILFM) and the Society of Law Accountants in Scotland (SOLAS) have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on professional education, knowledge sharing and events for legal finance and law accounting professionals. The agreement was reached a few weeks before being formally marked at the SOLAS AGM and Dinner in Edinburgh. Tim Kidd, ILFM chief executive, and SOLAS president David Hamilton commented.
stories.hook: ILFM and SOLAS sign memorandum of understanding to share education for legal finance professionals

stories.title: British lawyer among targets of convicted Iran spies
stories.ltme_summary: Two Iranian men, Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi Manesh, were convicted at Woolwich Crown Court of assisting a foreign intelligence service under the National Security Act 2023. Targets included barrister Jonathan Turner, chief executive of UK Lawyers for Israel. The CPS says Sepahvand was willing to commit serious violence. Sentencing is set for 17 December at the Central Criminal Court. A third defendant was acquitted.
stories.hook: Two Iranian men convicted of spying on critics of Tehran, including a London barrister

stories.ltme_summary: Perfect Portal has launched One Percent Payments, a payment service built with InfoTrack and powered by Mollie. It offers a 1 per cent handling charge on standard domestic credit and debit card payments for firms using both systems. The service is aimed at giving law firms another option for client payments.
stories.hook: Perfect Portal and InfoTrack launch 1% card payment service for conveyancing firms

stories.title: Getting the most from your case management system: why training and support matter
stories.ltme_summary: An article in Today's Conveyancer argues that buying a legal case management system is only the start, and that firms need training and support so staff understand the software and use it confidently. The extract is a short summary line with no vendor or firm named.
stories.hook: Training, not installation, decides whether a case management system pays off, says Today's Conveyancer

stories.title: Lost photos of fallen Kirkcaldy soldier unearthed after 80 years.
UKFIU SARs Annual Report 2026 – key messages
stories.ltme_summary: The UK Financial Intelligence Unit's SARs Annual Report 2026 reports 896,414 suspicious activity reports in 2025-26, up 3 per cent. It says a record £422.3m of criminal assets were denied through DAML requests. Raising the DAML threshold from £1,000 to £3,000 cut DAML submissions by 23 per cent. CILEx Regulation highlights implications for regulated firms, including law firms.
stories.hook: UKFIU annual report records 896,414 SARs and £422.3m of assets denied in 2025-26

stories.title: Using Reliable Matter Data for Effective Alternative Fee Arrangements
stories.ltme_summary: A blog post co-written by William Grady, director of information technology at Conn Kavanaugh Rosenthal Peisch and Ford LLP, and Sharon Scenna of Intapp, looks at using reliable matter data to support alternative fee arrangements. The authors argue that AFAs help firms give clients cost predictability while protecting profitability. The extract is the opening only and does not show the detailed guidance.
stories.hook: Conn Kavanaugh and Intapp argue reliable matter data is key to alternative fee arrangements
entities: Conn Kavanaugh Rosenthal Peisch & Ford LLP

stories.title: Billing & Finance Solutions for Law Firm Leaders | Elite

stories.ltme_summary: Elite, the Thomson Reuters legal billing and finance business, promotes its cloud-native 3E platform to law firm IT leaders. It claims 99.9 per cent uptime, SOC 2 Type II compliance, open APIs and a link to Microsoft Fabric. The page cites Gentry Locke going live on the cloud with 3E. The material is vendor marketing rather than independent assessment.

stories.title: Law Firm Software for Lawyers & Practice Leaders | Elite
stories.ltme_summary: Elite, the Thomson Reuters billing platform, markets its 3E cloud software to lawyers and practice leaders. It highlights passive time capture, automated proforma workflows and an AI-powered time entry tool called Elite Validate. The page cites Gentry Locke going live on the cloud with 3E and offers mobile access and client portals. The text is vendor promotion without independent evidence.
stories.hook: Elite promotes AI time entry tool Elite Validate for lawyers using its 3E billing platform

stories.title: Security & Compliance Software for Law Firms | Elite
stories.ltme_summary: Thomson Reuters Elite describes its SaaS platform's security and compliance features for law firms, including SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and GDPR support. The page is vendor marketing with no independent data.

stories.title: ROI Hub | The AI Financial Operations Platform for Law Firms
stories.ltme_summary: Thomson Reuters Elite promotes its ROI Hub and cloud migration material for law firms. It cites a Dentons executive on a go-live in under seven months and describes Data Connect delivery into Microsoft Fabric.

stories.title: Blogs & Research | The AI Financial Operations Platform for Law Firms
stories.ltme_summary: Thomson Reuters Elite's blog section argues that law firms moving from on-premises financial systems to cloud platforms are reporting gains in billing speed and cash flow. The piece is vendor thought leadership.

VANTAGE Philadelphia | The AI Financial Operations Platform for Law Firms | Elite
stories.ltme_summary: Thomson Reuters Elite is promoting VANTAGE Philadelphia, an event offering one-to-one sessions with Elite experts on 3E and eBillingHub. The page is an event invitation for law firm finance and IT teams.

stories.title: Elite Data Connect Honored By LegalTech Breakthrough With 2026 “Overall LegalTech Data Solution of the Year”
stories.ltme_summary: Elite says its Data Connect product has won the Overall LegalTech Data Solution of the Year award in the 2026 LegalTech Breakthrough Awards, announced on 12 November 2026. Data Connect feeds 3E, eBillingHub and Validate data into Microsoft Fabric. Mark Dorman, Elite's chief executive, says pilot customers report cutting reporting time by 50 per cent.
stories.hook: Elite's Data Connect wins LegalTech Breakthrough data award, with a claimed 50 per cent reporting cut

Most Legal Professionals Say AI Has Not Yet Changed Hiring, According to a Relativity Study
stories.ltme_summary: Relativity has released AI in Legal: 2026 Research Data, a study with IDC, finding 80.5 per cent of legal professionals use AI in legal work. 57.9 per cent of respondents said AI had no effect on hiring. The research covers 700 respondents across 20 nations, with IDC's study of 401. Doug Austin reproduces the vendor release.
stories.hook: Relativity study: 80.5% of legal professionals use AI, but most say hiring is unchanged

stories.title: In Monday’s November 2026 EDRM Case Law Webinar We’re Back and Better Than Ever!: eDiscovery Webinars
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin of eDiscovery Today previews the November 2026 EDRM case law webinar, to be held on Monday 16 November. Topics include sanctions for using AI to check email deletion schedules and discoverability of an expert's AI activity. Panellists include Tom O'Connor, Mary Mack and Hon. Andrew Peck of DLA Piper.
stories.hook: EDRM November webinar to cover AI sanctions and expert AI discoverability cases

stories.title: Mishcon de Reya advises UFORCE on $700 million Series A fundraising
stories.ltme_summary: Mishcon de Reya says it advised UFORCE, a defence technology company, on a $700 million Series A fundraising. Gunderson Dettmer worked with Mishcon on the US aspects of the deal.

When AI comes to the coroner's court
stories.ltme_summary: Weightmans considers how artificial intelligence may reach the coroner's court and what healthcare providers should prepare for now. The piece is a law firm commentary, with only its outline summary line visible in the extract.

stories.title: In Biglaw, Second Place Is Still Pretty Big
The Next Generation Of Law Students Don’t Trust AI Hype
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law reports on a Blickstein Group study of students at 37 colleges and universities, which found 71 per cent use AI several times a week for schoolwork. Students rate AI as a productivity aid rather than a trusted source, and the article argues this matters for legal tech adoption. The piece is commentary on the report.
stories.hook: Blickstein survey finds 71% of students use AI weekly, but few trust it for drafting

LSB launches review to avoid another Mazur crisis
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Board has launched a review of guidance on reserved legal activities other than conduct of litigation, following the Mazur fallout. The review covers rights of audience, conveyancing, probate, notarial activities and oaths. The LSB says the report should be published in January. Chief executive Richard Orpin is quoted.
stories.hook: LSB launches review of reserved-activity guidance to avoid another Mazur-style problem

stories.title: Iranian men convicted of spying on pro-Israel barrister
stories.ltme_summary: Two Iranian men were convicted at Woolwich Crown Court of assisting a foreign intelligence service after spying on a barrister and two Iran International journalists. Sepahvand and Manesh were found to be working for the IRGC. Jonathan Turner, a barrister who chairs Jewish Lawyers for Israel, was among the targets. A third defendant was acquitted.
stories.hook: Two Iranian men convicted of IRGC-linked spying on barrister Jonathan Turner and journalists

stories.title: Coulson persuaded not to speak out over Post Office slur
stories.ltme_summary: Sir Peter Coulson, a retired Court of Appeal judge, writes in his new book The Practice of Judging that he was persuaded by the Lady Chief Justice and the Master of the Rolls not to respond publicly to claims that he backed Mr Justice Fraser's refusal to recuse himself in the Post Office litigation. He calls the 2019 recusal application rubbish and criticises counsel's conduct during the Sir Wyn Williams inquiry.
stories.hook: Sir Peter Coulson says he was talked out of responding to Post Office claims about Mr Justice Fraser

stories.title: SRA urged to investigate law firm over Walliams letter
stories.ltme_summary: The Good Law Project has called on the Solicitors Regulation Authority to investigate Schillings' work for David Walliams. The call follows Guardian and ITV reporting of allegations against the author, and a 2016 letter from Schillings to a young woman that threatened her with an offence if she spoke out. Schillings says it was instructed to write the letter and disputes the characterisation of its correspondence.
stories.hook: Good Law Project urges SRA to investigate Schillings over a 2016 letter sent for David Walliams

stories.title: SRA finalises how it plans to ‘reset’ and focus on “proactive, intelligence led’ regulation
stories.ltme_summary: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has published its final 2026/27 Business Plan, setting out chief executive Sarah Rapson's plan to reset the regulator. The plan was first launched in May and was widely consulted on. The outlet says one of its more controversial points was a 29 per cent cut, though the extract does not say what the cut applies to. The plan focuses on proactive, intelligence-led regulation.
stories.hook: SRA publishes final 2026/27 Business Plan to reset the regulator around intelligence-led regulation

stories.ltme_summary: RPC's knowledge lawyers Aimee Talbot and Jonathan Wyles examine professional indemnity risks for solicitors who use generative AI, and those who do not. They cite the UKJT statement on AI harms and rising AI-drafted complaints.

LawFairy launches app for legal assessments
stories.ltme_summary: LawFairy, a regulated law firm, has launched Trusted Legal Intelligence, a rules-based app giving immigration assessments for a fixed fee of £149. Users answer a questionnaire and can be connected to a solicitor the same day. CEO Raj Panasar says the app has already supported LawFairy's first successful visa application. The launch is company-described.

stories.title: Banks' AI access ban warns firms
stories.ltme_summary: Shieldpay, a payments provider working with more than 40 top UK law firms, warns that banks including HSBC and Barclays have restricted AI agents from accessing customer accounts. Its chief technology officer, Simon Goodyear, says uptake of AI among law firms is creating risks for client money, particularly where bots process payments beyond their mandates. He expects agents to authorise payments in future and urges firms to review SRA technology guidance.
stories.hook: Shieldpay warns law firms that banks restricting AI agents signal risks for client money handling

stories.title: Post Office case highlights further software flaws pre-Horizon
stories.ltme_summary: The Criminal Cases Review Commission has referred a third conviction linked to Post Office software to the Court of Appeal, after evidence that the earlier Capture accounting system could also produce errors. Narinder Aujla, who was convicted of theft in 1998 after a £10,000 shortfall at his Dudley branch, applied to the CCRC in June 2025. The CCRC says it has received 40 applications linked to pre-Horizon cases.
stories.hook: CCRC refers a third Post Office conviction to the Court of Appeal over the earlier Capture system

stories.hook: Podcast guest Elizabeth Botsford discusses why the legal sector may need its own large language model

stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer's weekly wrap reports that Twin1 AI raised a $5 million Seed extension, taking its total to $25 million. Other items include Chamelio hires, a Clio move to Manchester and a Harbor acquisition of AAC Consulting.

Iranian men convicted over spying on barrister and journalists
stories.ltme_summary: Two Iranian men, Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi Manesh, have been convicted at Woolwich Crown Court of assisting a foreign intelligence service by spying on a UK barrister and journalists. Sentencing is set for 17 December 2026.

stories.title: Could using ChatGPT cost you a training contract?
Is your legal work “too complex” for AI?
stories.ltme_summary: A LexisNexis column for Legal Futures says a survey of private practice lawyers in large firms found four-fifths use AI for legal research, and about two-thirds use it for knowledge management and document work. Only 30 per cent say AI is embedded in their team's strategy and operations. Travers Smith's chief technology officer Oliver Bethell is quoted on bespoke work.
stories.hook: LexisNexis survey finds four-fifths of large-firm lawyers use AI for research but only 30% have embedded it

stories.title: Partner was expelled due to “intimate relationship” with junior
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures reports that an employment tribunal ruled Clintons was not discriminating when it expelled partner Kami Naghdi in 2023. Judge Emma Webster, in a 107-page ruling, found the expulsion followed his relationships with junior staff. Naghdi has applied to appeal to the Employment Appeal Tribunal.
stories.hook: Tribunal finds Clintons expelled partner over junior relationships, not discrimination

stories.title: 'Off to the pub': Lawyers react as Microsoft Outlook outage brings down emails
stories.ltme_summary: Lawyers worldwide reported email disruption from an ongoing Microsoft Outlook outage, which the BBC says affected Microsoft 365 services in 74 countries. Firms issued client notices and turned to phone calls.

stories.title: Blast off: Charles Russell Speechlys advises on £30m UK spaceport funding
Ex-Cravath employee charged over insider trading tied to major client M&A deals
Ex-Kingsley Napley director suspended for inappropriate behaviour
stories.ltme_summary: The Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal suspended Andrew Cane Solomon, a former legal director at Kingsley Napley, from practice for 36 months. He admitted non-consensual touching of a trainee at a 2023 work event.

stories.title: ACL conference: Costs lawyers upbeat about AI threat but clients demand savings
stories.ltme_summary: The Association of Costs Lawyers annual conference in London heard that clients are pressing costs lawyers to pass AI efficiencies into invoices. Speakers including Lady Justice Cockerill and Joanne Powell of the Government Legal Department discussed the limits of AI in costs work. The Law Society's updated guidance on billing for AI-assisted time is cited, and in-house voices from Lloyds Banking Group and Compass Group add client views.
stories.hook: Costs lawyers hear clients want AI savings passed on in invoices

stories.title: LSB opens review to see off potential for another Mazur
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Board has launched a review of frontline regulators' guidance on reserved legal activities, following the Mazur litigation. The review covers rights of audience, probate, notarial activities and oaths, with a report expected in January.

stories.title: Partner's removal over affair conduct was not discrimination, tribunal rules
stories.ltme_summary: The Employment Tribunal at London Central has dismissed barrister Kamir Naghdi's claims against Clintons Legal and its partners, finding his 2023 expulsion from the equity partnership was not discrimination. The judge found the firm expelled him over his conduct towards a junior colleague. Naghdi has the right to seek an appeal, according to a related report.
stories.hook: Tribunal rules Clintons' expulsion of former equity partner was not discrimination

stories.title: Huge rise in solicitors refusing to reveal sex and race
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society's Annual Statistics Report 2026 shows the number of practising certificate holders who did not disclose their sex rose from 12,358 to 36,094 between 2022 and 2025. Non-disclosure of ethnicity rose from 38,947 to 61,360. The roll stood at 208,077 by July 2025. The Society says the gaps limit conclusions about diversity.
stories.hook: Law Society figures show solicitors not disclosing sex or ethnicity has risen sharply since 2022

stories.title: Legal Services Board makes policy and performance appointments
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Board has announced three senior appointments to strengthen its ability to hold legal services regulators to account. The outlet names Shona Barton as Director, Regulatory, among the appointments. The extract does not list the other two appointees.
stories.hook: Legal Services Board names Shona Barton as Director, Regulatory, among three senior appointments

stories.title: Law Society welcomes CJC’s AI report but warns of potential for ‘misleading documents’
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society of England and Wales has responded to the Civil Justice Council's report on preparing court documents with AI. It warns of the potential for misleading documents, particularly where people represent themselves in court. Law Society president Brett Dixon is quoted. The response welcomes the report while raising that concern.
stories.hook: Law Society welcomes CJC AI report but warns of misleading court documents
entities: Law Society of England and Wales

stories.title: Compass launches national SDLT survey
stories.ltme_summary: Property tax specialist Compass has launched a national survey inviting conveyancing professionals to take part. The survey examines how law firms manage Stamp Duty Land Tax, identify complex transactions and protect clients against errors. The outlet summary gives no results or closing date.
stories.hook: Compass launches national survey on how conveyancers manage Stamp Duty Land Tax

Microsoft 365 Service Disruption
Ready for growth? The questions every law firm should be asking
stories.ltme_summary: Osprey Approach and Legal News Wales have published the Welsh Legal Sector Transformation Report 2026, drawing on more than 50 firms and in-house teams in Wales. It finds that 42 per cent of firms lack a succession plan and that billing write-offs average just under 14 per cent. The report also finds that over 94 per cent of firms have core systems, while billing is seen as the most inefficient process.
stories.hook: Osprey Approach survey finds Welsh firms write off almost 14% of billing
